P1.evidence: Setter notes were mentioned but never used: 'I already got some information from Derek, but I would just love to hear everything from you.' Nothing specific was read back. No four-part frame — a fit frame only. Agreement obtained. Open question asked verbatim: 'So, tell me, like, what can we potentially help you out with?'

P2.evidence: P2d was the strongest work on the call: 'you're saying yourself, like, you have some pains here and there, flare up as you get older, and that's normal, I can tell you it's not normal. So what's sort of the pains or things that you sometimes have flaring up for yourself?' produced the AC joint, both elbows, the shoulder and the knee with timeframes. Nutrition was asked. Age was asked. But height and weight were never asked, health conditions were never asked, training days were never established, sleep and energy were never asked, and the rep guessed his occupation wrongly — 'you're 36, you work in tech' — when the prospect had said he is a creative producer for television.

P3.evidence: The bridge was asked well — 'Why do you want to constantly have those challenges for yourself? Like, what's the reason for you to constantly do that?' — and the answer that came back was novelty: 'I want to do something new... it just makes me excited.' The rep accepted it and reflected it back as the why. He never asked what better movement would do for him, never asked who else it impacts, and never drove to family, identity or longevity. On the most price-resistant prospect in the batch, the deepest reason established was that he gets bored, which is not a reason worth $4,000.

P4.evidence: Past attempts were probed properly and at length — the three competing companies, the Australian programme, the calisthenics offer, the UK trainer. But the actual failure in his history, that muscle he builds deflates within three months of stopping, was never asked about. And P4f was inverted: the rep repeatedly agreed the prospect does not need help — 'you already have the discipline, don't you?' and 'You've done it for so long, you know what you're talking about, of course' — which removed the reason to buy.

P5.evidence: Entirely skipped. No two-year picture, no willingness-to-settle test, no why-not, no line in the sand. This is the prospect with unresolved bilateral tennis elbow, a permanent AC joint separation and an explicit plan to keep going alone — 'let's try to do it by myself. Maybe I get hurt, maybe I don't' — and none of it was ever turned into a consequence.

P6.evidence: No commitment was secured before presenting. The per-pillar fit checks — 'Do you feel like, yeah, this makes sense to me, and I see myself doing it like that?' — test comprehension, not commitment. The isolation came after the price rather than before: 'outside of the money part, right? Do you feel like this is actually what I see myself doing?' The offer was delivered into an announced eight-minute hard stop.

P11.evidence: No close was attempted. No payment was requested, no link was sent. The call ended on a proposal to reconvene.

objection_plays.detail: One isolation ran — 'outside of the money part, right? Do you feel like this is actually what I see myself doing?' — and nothing else. No financial picture at all: no cash on hand, no monthly leftover, no credit cards, no available credit, no investments. No payment plan was offered. Instead of running the play the rep shortened the term and quoted a new price, which answers a commitment objection with a discount structure.

Trigger clear: 'I can think about this. I'm going to really dive mind-wise and then get back to you' and 'I need to think if it's something that I wanted to commit to it.' No scripted move ran — no 'do you feel what we've gone through CAN get you to your goal', no 'what's actually coming up that's preventing you from getting started', no 'thinking isn't the problem, deciding is'. The rep booked a follow-up instead.

The deciding objection has no scripted play: a cheap alternative that has genuinely worked for twenty years — self-programming plus Planet Fitness at $28 a month — set against a lifestyle-spend comparison at $275-300 a month for a high-end gym with a spa. This is the documented gap in the script. The rep asked one good challenge question and then conceded: 'if you're looking for a cheaper price, then he's definitely not the fit in that sense.'

A second script gap: the prospect will not commit to a six-month term on something he has not felt in his own body, and asked repeatedly for three months. The offer has only six and twelve month tiers and there is no play for a term-length objection, so the rep improvised a $4,000 three-month price on the call.

A third gap: process friction. He objected to app logging and video submission before the pillars were delivered — 'I have to spend an hour to take a picture, to take a video, to send it. And I know that's how you guys work' — the rep deflected with a joke and then presented that exact model unchanged.

notes: Phase 5 was skipped entirely and Phase 6 never happened, so the price landed on a prospect whose stated reason to buy was that he gets bored. The most damaging pattern is agreement: across Phase 4 the rep repeatedly confirmed the prospect does not need coaching, which is warm and true and removed the case for a $4,000 purchase. Second correction: the prospect announced an eight-minute hard stop before the presentation and the rep compressed the offer and the price into it rather than taking the rebook he had already offered.
